līlāmūrtis
(‘aspects of [Śiva] in various forms’)
------------------------------------------
Though शिव, the third aspect of the Hindu Trinity, is worshipped only as a लिङ्ग in the temples, twenty five forms of his are mentioned in the iconographical works. These forms (in human shapes) are established separately as decorative motifs, but, not worshipped.
Some of them are: Anugrahamūrtis (bestowing grace upon devotees like नन्दि, रावण or Caṇḍeśa); Antakamūrtis (des-troying the demons like गजासुर or Tripuras); Nṛttamūrtis (in the dancing pose like tāṇḍava dance); दक्षिणामूर्ति (in the teaching pose of a गुरु); Haryardhamūrti (combined form of Hari and Hara); Ardhanārīśvara (combined form of शिव and पार्वती); Bhikṣāṭana-mūrti (as a mendicant with a begging bowl) and so on.

Līlāśuka
------------------------------------------
The long hymn Śrīkṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta, is an extremely popular hymn extolling the doings and the greatness of Lord कृष्ण. Its author is लीलाशुक. Whether it was his real name or the pen-name, is difficult to say. Some identify him with the devotee Bilvamaṅgal.
Since श्रीकृष्ण चैतन्य (A.

-1533) is said to have brought a copy of this book from South India, he must have lived before the 15th century.
He was a disciple of Somagiri and might have got his general एदुचतिओन् from Śikhipiñcha. Though a Śaiva by birth, कृष्ण was his chosen deity. He probably belonged to the Āndhradeśa (the present Andhra Pradesh).
Some popular stories picture him as having become an ascetic after being admonished by a harlot, चिन्तामणि by name, to whom he was terribly attached.
